In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rAOB/rNOb value of a STP is not solely determined by the AOB/NOB relative abundance.

the rAOB/rNOb ratio is a function of the wastewater characteristics and the process conditions, and that it is not possible to generalize the factors that control the rAOB/NOb ratio in different STPs.
inorganic carbon and nitrogen loading rate are the main parameters controlling rAOB/rNOb in sewage treatment plants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AOB to rNOB activity ratio in STP can be influenced by wastewater and process parameters.

the AOB to rNOB activity ratios are determined by both the wastewater composition (e.g. inorganic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus) and the operational conditions (e.g. sludge retention time, temperature).
AOB and NOBs are both limited by the same factors, but the degree of limitation is different.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activity of nitrifying bacteria is not only determined by the community composition, but also by the availability of limiting nutrients.
a high rAOB/rNOD ratio is possible in full-scale STP's and is not necessarily limited by temperature, but by other factors.
the AOB to rNOB activity ratio is a dynamic parameter that can be influenced by wastewater and process parameters.
